oneOf.description: Astrid runs it. Nothing to set up.
The account's own agent asks for work.
The account's own agent is told about work.
It does not run.

Attachment.description: A legacy file attachment. Superseded by [`SecureFile`]; still returned on older tasks.

virtualKey.description: Set for the channels that belong to a virtual list rather than a stored one.

authorId.description: Absent on the messages the server authors itself.

type.description: The same TEXT/MARKDOWN/ATTACHMENT enum comments use.

authorId.description: Absent on system comments, which the server authors itself.

clientRequestId.description: The server echoes the `temp_<uuid>` idempotency key back. Offline dedup depends on it.

id.description:
Mutable because an offline comment is created with a `temp_` id and keeps its identity when
the server's id arrives.

remoteAuthorLogin.description:
The GitHub login of a commenter with no Astrid account (AWTD-1283). Set only when
`author_id` and `author` are both absent, and it makes the comment a person's, not the
server's — see [`Comment::is_system`].

remoteNodeId.description:
The GitHub comment this one mirrors, on a GitHub Projects deployment (AWTD-1283).
Informational only.

CustomRepeatingPattern.description:
The custom repeat pattern, kept as loose as it is on the wire.

Every field is optional because the shape depends on `unit` and the server has never validated
the combination. Interpretation lives in [`crate::repeating`] and nowhere else.

DeleteTaskMode.description:
`list.supports.deleteTask`. A GitHub board takes the item off the project and leaves the issue.
A value this build does not know reads as the classic one.

DueDraft.description: The due date an editor holds, ahead of the cache (AITD-461).

ListAgentConfig.description:
`{ enabledTypes, defaultAgentId, allowMemberAssignment }` — the shape the server stores and,
since 2026-08-29, emits as `aiAgentConfig` beside the plain `aiAgentsEnabled` array. It carries
the default agent the array cannot express.

allowMemberAssignment.description:
Whether a member, rather than only an admin, may assign a task to an agent on this list.

Carried so the wire round trip loses nothing; nothing in the core reads it yet, and gating
on it is a dispatch decision rather than a model one. `Option` rather than `bool` because
absent and `false` are different answers, and defaulting the key in would invent it on a
surface that never sent it.

ListMember.description: Someone's membership of a list. Presence IS membership; the role only refines what it allows.

id.description:
Absent in the embedded member arrays some responses return (creating a task, for one), and
the user id stands in — see [`ListMember::identity`].

ListRemote.description:
`list.remote`: which GitHub Project a GitHub-backed list mirrors (web
`lib/backends/list-wire.ts`).

The counterpart of [`super::task::TaskRemote`] one level up, and a simpler shape: web fills all
three keys or sends `null` for the whole object, never a partial one — `null` for a classic
list, for an iteration list, which is a tag rather than a bound board, and for a board whose
GitHub installation row has gone. They are still `#[serde(default)]`, for the same reason every
field in this module is: a thinner payload from a server this build does not know must not fail
the whole list.

number.description: The project's number in that account, which is how GitHub itself names it.

owner.description: The GitHub account the project belongs to: an organisation's login, or a person's.

ListSupports.description:
`list.supports` on the wire: what a list's backend can do that a client would otherwise have
to guess. Every key is at its classic value when absent, and the web adds a key as each
capability lands (`lib/backends/supports.ts`) — so a key this build does not know is ignored
rather than refused.

deleteTask.description: What deleting a task does here.

dueDate.description: A due date can be set. False on a GitHub board with no date field mapped.

fields.description: Tasks here can carry the project's own field values (web AWTD-1208).

membership.description: Members and invitations are managed in Astrid. On a GitHub board the roster is GitHub's.

multipleAssignees.description: A task here may hold several assignees (`assigneeIds`). Classic lists keep at most one.

priority.description: Priority can be set. False on a GitHub board with no Priority field mapped.

privateTasks.description: `isPrivate` means something here. A GitHub board's tasks are as visible as its project.

repeatMode.description: How a repeating task here advances when it is completed (web AWTD-1118, spec §10).

PendingDeletion.description: A remote twin still waiting to be removed.

Preferences.description:
What My Tasks is filtered and sorted by, for this account, on every device.

Held by the account rather than the machine, which is the whole reason this exists as its own
endpoint: filters set on a laptop are the filters on the desktop.

filterAssignee.description:
Carried so a write keeps what another client stored; never applied — iOS's My Tasks does
not read it, and its scope already is "assigned to me" (D25).

filterPriority.description: Empty means every priority — see the module note.

Priority.description:
How urgent, 0-3.

**Decoded leniently.** The server's schema puts no cap on `priority`, and two production tasks
were observed carrying `4`. Swift's default enum decode threw on those, which failed the decode
of the WHOLE tasks array and silently broke sync for that account. An unknown value reads as
[`Priority::None`] so the task stays usable.

customStates.description:
The board's own columns, and renames of the three defaults.

Free-form JSON on the wire, and read rather than typed: an entry a newer web writes must not
stop a board drawing. [`crate::board::parse_custom_states`] is the only place that reads it.

key.description:
The prefix this project's task identifiers carry — `AWTD` in `AWTD-1007`.

Unique across astrid.cc, and `None` for a project made before identifiers existed. The
server is the only minter; this is read so a client knows which keys the reader can see,
which is what decides whether `AWTD-1007` in a comment becomes a link
([`crate::identifier::find_links`], task 5f3453e2).

id.description: Omitted by the embedded member arrays, like [`super::list::ListMember`].

RecentlyCompletedWindow.description:
How far back "Recently completed" reaches for one list.

Mirrors `astrid-web/lib/recently-completed-window.ts`, discriminated by `kind`. The same
setting drives the list view's default completion filter and the board's Done column, so the
two views can never disagree. `None` on the list means the legacy 24-hour default.

RepeatFromMode.description: Whether the next occurrence is measured from the due date or from when it was actually done.

RepeatMode.description:
`list.supports.repeatMode`. On a GitHub board the completed issue stays closed as history and
the next occurrence is a NEW task the server makes, so a client sends the completion and does
not roll the row forward itself. A value this build does not know reads as the classic one:
rolling forward is recoverable, a series silently dropped is not.

SecureFile.description:
A file held by the server's secure-file store. The wire names differ from the field names, and
those aliases are the whole reason this type is hand-mapped.

SyncMode.description:
How lists get linked.

Stored on the server in the integration's metadata, so the choice follows the account rather
than the machine.

oneOf.description: One list at a time, chosen by hand.
Every remote list mirrors in; new ones are picked up each pass.
Every Astrid list mirrors out; new ones are picked up each pass.
Both, with same-name pairs adopting each other rather than duplicating.

assigneeIds.description:
Everyone assigned, as the server sent it (web AWTD-1190). Only a list whose backend
supports several assignees ever holds more than one. Never read this directly:
[`Task::all_assignee_ids`] is the list a client shows, because `assignee_id` is written on
its own — by an older client, or by an optimistic reassignment here — and stays the truth
about who is first.

blockedBy.description:
The tasks this one is waiting on, by id, and the tasks waiting on it.

`GET /api/v1/tasks/:id` adds both beside `listIds`, and the wire contract
(`astrid-web/lib/api-contracts/v1-ios-shapes.ts`, `V1TaskBlockerIds`) makes them
**optional** so the server and each client ship independently: a deployment older than the
feature simply does not send them, which reads here as "nothing known", never as "nothing".

Ids only. The titles a chip draws come from `GET /api/v1/tasks/:id/blockers`, because a
blocker the reader cannot see has an id and nothing else — and the difference between that
and a blocker that merely has not synced yet is the one thing the row must not get wrong.
Needs no cache migration: the store keeps each model's whole JSON and lifts out only the
columns something queries.

closedReason.description:
Why the task was closed, when it was closed as anything but done: `canceled` |
`duplicate` | `not_planned` (web task 11042ae3). The web keeps `completed` true beside it,
so every view that reads the flag keeps working; only the rendering and the repeat rollover
differ. Kept as text rather than an enum so a reason this build has never heard of cannot
make the whole task unreadable.

completedAt.description: The real completion time, which sync may backdate.

creatorId.description:
The MCP API returns the creator object without the id field, so both are optional and
[`Task::effective_creator_id`] is the only correct way to ask.

description.description:
`None` is **the response did not say** — `GET /api/v1/tasks?omit=description` leaves the
key out and names it in `meta.omitted` — and `Some("")` is a description a person cleared.
They were one `""` until task ebe0966b (D55), which meant any write built from a cached row
erased text somebody had typed. [`Task::keeping_unsent`] fills an omitted one from the
cache; [`Task::description_text`] is what a reader that only draws or searches it wants.

dueDateTime.description:
The single source of truth for when the task is due. See [`super::date`] for what this
means when [`Task::is_all_day`] is set.

fields.description:
This task's GitHub project field VALUES, keyed by `ProjectField.id` (web AWTD-1208, spec
§9.4.3). No names and no types: those come once per project from
`GET /api/v1/projects/:id/fields`.

**`None` means "not asked", never "none".** The list route carries values only on
`?include=fields`, because a thousand tasks' worth is 42.2 KiB over an already tight
payload budget, while the task-detail route always carries them — and a task with no
values carries no key at all (web `lib/tasks/v1-task-fields.ts`). Those three cases are
indistinguishable here, so nothing may read an absent map as "this task has no field
values".

Which is why this is NOT where a pane reads them from:
`astrid_core::services::project_fields` caches the values under a key of their own, since
`store::upsert_task` replaces the whole encoded task and one list page fetched without
`?include=fields` would otherwise wipe what a detail fetch knew. What the key is modelled
FOR is the round trip — a value is only safe to cache and pass on once it survives a
decode and a re-encode, which is what task faa32e20 found it did not.

Values are `string | number` on the wire. They stay [`serde_json::Value`] because that is
already how a field value is represented where it is typed and validated
(`project_fields::accepts`), and two representations of one scalar is one too many.

identifier.description:
The human-readable id — `AST-142` (web task 12f54df4). Minted by the server for tasks on
a project; absent for a task on a project-less list, so a solo user never sees one.
Searchable as a direct hit.

isAllDay.description:
Defaults to **true**, matching the Swift memberwise init: a task created with a date and no
stated time is an all-day task.

nextOccurrenceId.description:
The occurrence that followed this one (web AWTD-1219). Only the single-task read and the
row beside a live event carry the key — an id, or `null` for "none" — and a list page
leaves it out. So absent (`None`) is "this response does not say", which
[`Task::keeping_unsent`] fills from the cache, and `Some(None)` is the server saying there
is no successor. Encodes back as it arrived, because the cache keeps the whole JSON.

originalTaskId.description: Copy lineage - the task this one was copied from. NOT the subtask relation.

parentTaskId.description:
Subtasks: the parent's id, `None` for a top-level task. A self-relation on the server,
nulled when the parent is deleted.

previousOccurrenceId.description:
The occurrence this one followed, on a list whose series spawns a new task each time
(web AWTD-1118). The link back; the way forward is the task that names this one here.

remote.description:
The GitHub issue or pull request a task on a GitHub board is (web AWTD-1222, spec §11.2).
Only a GitHub-backed task carries it; absent means classic.

statusRole.description:
Board status as a state ON the task: `ready` | `doing` | `waiting` | a project's custom
role. `None` means Inbox; Done is derived from `completed`, so neither is ever stored.

Tolerated as absent on purpose (task AWTD-562): a deployment older than the field simply
does not send it, and the board falls back to list membership. That fallback is what keeps
this build working against an unmigrated server.

syncState.description:
Where the server's write-back to the list's backend stands (web spec §11.2): `pending`
while a task made on a GitHub board is still being written there, `error` if that gave
up. Absent and `null` are both "settled" — it is a column on the task, so every response
carries it, and `null` is what a settled task and every classic list send.

admins.description:
Legacy denormalised arrays. Kept so the public-lists endpoint still decodes; **never**
consulted for a role — see [`crate::permissions`].

aiAgentsEnabled.description:
Accepts both the documented `string[]` and the object form the server once leaked. See the
module note.

backend.description:
Which backend holds this list (web AWTD-1256, spec §11.2): `"github_project"` for a GitHub
Projects board, `null` for a classic one. Ask through [`TaskList::is_github_backed`].

privacy.description: Absent from the thinner responses, so never assume a missing privacy means private.

projectId.description:
Project status board. A project holds both `listType: "regular"` (domain) lists and
`listType: "status"` (board column) lists. Inbox and Done are virtual columns derived from
task state and are never stored.

remote.description:
The GitHub Project this list mirrors (web AWTD-1222, spec §11.2), for the board's own chip
and its "open on GitHub". **`None` means there is no page**, which a classic list, an
iteration list and a board whose installation has gone all share — see [`ListRemote`].

showSubtasks.description: **`None` means SHOW.** See the module note and [`TaskList::shows_subtasks`].

supports.description:
What this list's backend can do (web AWTD-1190, spec §11.2). **`None` means classic**: a
server older than the field omits it. Ask through the methods, not the field.

TaskRemote.description: `task.remote`: where a task on a GitHub board lives on GitHub (web `lib/backends/task-remote.ts`).

url.description: The issue or pull request on GitHub. `None` for a draft, which has no page of its own.

oneOf.description: The brand look: light, with a cyan surface. The default.
Whatever the system is set to.

TitleDisplay.description: How much of a row's title is shown.

oneOf.description: As many lines as the title needs. The default (DS19).
Two lines, then an ellipsis. What the Mac and Windows did before there was a choice.
One line, then an ellipsis. The densest list.

TriggerKind.description: Which kind of thing a trigger asks for.

defaultDueTime.description: `HH:MM`, the time of day a new all-day task defaults to when the user gives it a time.

email.description: Optional: the public-lists endpoint returns admins without their email addresses.

verified.description:
The account's own verification state, as `GET /users/me` merges it into the user (task
19fd9289): verified outright or through a sign-in provider, whether a change of address is
waiting, and what it is. Only ever present on the signed-in user; absent on everyone else,
and absent from a server older than the fields.

oneOf.description: Every list, for the sidebar.
One list.

The rows to draw for a list, already filtered, sorted, spliced and projected.

One command rather than "give me the tasks, and here is how I will filter them": the
filtering, the sort, the subtask splice and the row projection are four contracts, and a
shell that ran them itself would be four chances to disagree with web.

currentUserId.description: Who is signed in, as the shell knows it.

idsOnly.description:
Answer with the ids in order (`ids`) instead of projected rows: for a shell that draws its
own rows from tasks it already holds, the projection is work nobody reads.

limit.description:
How many rows are wanted. Absent means all of them — which is the right answer for a
list of forty and the wrong one for a list of ten thousand.

list.description:
The list itself: one the cache does not hold (a public list the reader is not in), or a
shape with no row behind it (iOS's everything view: every task, the default completion
window, the priority sort).

myTasks.description: My Tasks' filters as the shell holds them.

offset.description: Where to start, for a virtualised list. Absent means the beginning.

sortBy.description:
A sort chosen on this device for a view that has no list row to save one on — the Mac's
sort menu over My Tasks. Wins over the list's and the account's.

tasks.description: The tasks to draw from instead of the cache's — that public list's, fetched on demand.

oneOf.description:
How many tasks each list's saved filters keep — the sidebar's number for a saved filter
(AITD-460). Sourced as `rowsForList` sources: every cached task for a virtual list, its
members for a real one. Subtasks count, because they are tasks the filters kept.

The sidebar's numbers as iOS's ListTaskCount draws them (AATD-39): a list's open tasks, a
saved filter what its filters keep (as `listCounts`), a public list the server's count, and
— under `my_tasks_id` — the open tasks assigned to the reader.

The sidebar, whole: My Tasks, the favourites and the rest of the places, each in order and
carrying the badge `listBadges` would give it (task e22621e2).

One command rather than three calls and a filter, because "which of these is somewhere to
go" is a product question and every shell had been answering it in its own language —
Android's answer (`SidebarViewModel.kt`) hid board columns and labels but offered GitHub
milestones and iterations as lists you could file a task into. The rule is
`astrid_rules::rows::sidebar::sections`.

currentUserId.description:
Whose My Tasks badge to count. Absent means the signed-in reader, which is what a
sidebar wants; it is here because `listBadges` takes it and a test must be able to say.

oneOf.description: One task in full, for the detail view.

Cached tasks in their wire shape: every one, or those named (a temporary id reads as the
task it became). For a shell that keeps its own models and filters them itself — the Apple
apps' views bind to `[Task]` — rather than drawing this crate's rows.

Everything one task's detail screen needs: the task, its comments, its subtasks, its list
chips, and the order to lay the fields out in.

One command rather than five, because the field order is a cross-platform product decision
and a shell that assembled the screen itself would be the fifth place to get it wrong.

The quick date and time choices for a task, with the instant each one means and which
one it is already set to.

Resolved here rather than in the shell because the arithmetic is the part that goes wrong:
a day is 23 or 25 hours across a daylight-saving boundary, an all-day date is stored
differently from a timed one, and "morning" means 09:00 where the reader is rather than in
UTC. Three clients read the same list in the same order — see `astrid_core::rows::due_picks`.
What a chosen calendar day means for this task, as an instant.

A calendar hands back a DAY; whether that is a date or a date-and-time depends on the task,
and an all-day date written as a local midnight reads back as the day before west of UTC.
So the shell asks rather than computes — the same reason the quick picks carry their
instants. See `rows::due_picks::on_day`.

day.description: The calendar day the reader clicked, as `YYYY-MM-DD`.

oneOf.description:
A time of day from a picker (24-hour), on the task's own day, as a timed due date — answers
`{ dueDateTime, isAllDay: false }` like a quick pick (AATD-25).

Taking the time off a task: all-day, on the day it was already showing (task 0616f2d1).

The other half of [`Command::DueDateAtTime`], and it cannot be the shell writing
`{ dueDateTime: <the instant it had>, isAllDay: true }` — nothing normalises that pair, and
an all-day date is read as its UTC day, so a task due in the evening west of UTC would move
to tomorrow. Answers `{ dueDateTime, isAllDay: true }` like a quick pick; a task with no
date has no day to keep and answers a null date rather than inventing today.

A date pick is the reader's calendar day as an all-day date, at UTC midnight, whatever the
task held — iOS's quick date (AITD-461, `docs/CONTRACTS.md` D48). An editor holding a date
the cache has not got yet (unsaved, or a task not created yet) sends it as `draft`.
A task's comments.

Refresh what one task is waiting on, from the server (task 69a840a4).

`TaskDetail` already answers with whatever is cached, so the row draws before this returns
and still draws with no network at all. This is the round trip that corrects it — and the
only thing that can tell "a task you cannot see" from "a task this cache has not got yet",
since the ids on the task cannot say which.

Make one task wait on another.

Optimistic and journalled, like every other write. The server moves statuses off the back
of it — a Ready task with a new blocker becomes Waiting — and those arrive as ordinary task
updates. No client writes `statusRole` for this. To *move* a task to Waiting on a task in
one gesture, send the move with `waitOnTaskId` ([`WaitOptions`]).

A GitHub board's project fields for one task, schema and values (AITD-491; web AWTD-1210).

Shaped like [`Command::TaskBlockers`]: the round trip that refreshes the cache, which
answers with what is cached when offline. No rows on a task off a GitHub board.
Set one project field; `value: null` clears it. Sent at once, journalled only when offline.

What the "Wait on a task…" picker may offer for a query.

The search is the SERVER's (`GET /api/v1/search`), which is permission-filtered in the
query — unlike [`Command::SearchTasks`], which reads this machine's cache. A picker that
filtered a loaded page locally would offer only what happened to be on screen, which is
the bug web fixed as `5df85b9f`. Two characters is the threshold; below it the answer is
empty rather than everything.

Find a task by what it says.

Over the cache, which is where every client searches: there is no server search endpoint,
and the Apple service's "online" path reads the same cached array its offline path does.
So this is instant, works on a train, and is the same set of rules everywhere.

The rules are iOS's search box (`services::search::search_tasks`, AITD-459): one phrase as
typed, from the first character, top-level tasks, completed work as a list shows it by
default unless `includeCompleted` says otherwise, highest priority first.

showSubtasks.description: The open list's own subtask setting, which iOS's search splice also honours.

subtaskDisplay.description:
Splice each result's subtasks in under it, as iOS's list draws search results
(AITD-460): given, with the account's display mode, the subtasks follow the default
completion window. Absent, the results are flat — the Mac's search, and web's.

oneOf.description:
The board a list belongs to: its columns, and the cards in each.

Answers with rows, so a card draws like a row — see [`crate::board`] for why a column id is
a role rather than a list id.

The cards are iOS's (AITD-461, `docs/CONTRACTS.md` D43): top-level tasks only, in the
opened list's manual order, with Done holding recent work as that list's completion filter
and window say. Every card comes back unless `limit` asks for a window.

idsOnly.description: Each column's card ids rather than rows — for a shell that draws its own copies.

limit.description: How many cards to carry per column. The count comes back whole.

listId.description:
The list the board was opened from: its project is the board, and its manual order
and Done window arrange the cards.

projectId.description:
The board itself, for a shell that knows the project but holds no list of it yet.
The opened list's project wins when both are given.

oneOf.description:
Drop a card at a slot in a column (AITD-461): the move a drag makes, plus the card's new
place in the opened list's manual order — what iOS's board drop writes.

Unlike [`Command::MoveTaskToColumn`], a drop onto the card's own column is not a no-op:
it is how a column is rearranged.

index.description:
The slot among the column's cards as the board drew them: 0 is the top, the column's
length the bottom.

listId.description: The list the board was opened from, whose manual order the drop rearranges.

oneOf.description:
Move a card to a column.

Into Waiting, the move needs a wait condition and clears the assignee — see [`WaitOptions`]
for the optional `dueDateTime` / `isAllDay` / `waitOnTaskId` / `keepAssignee`, and for the
`WAITING_NEEDS_CONDITION` refusal.

listId.description:
The list the board was opened from, so the move knows which project's columns to
resolve the target against.

oneOf.description:
Add a card at the bottom of a column (task 95c7a68f).

One request, not a create followed by a move: the column decides the card's lists, its role
and — for Done — that it is finished, and [`crate::board::resolve_create`] is what says so.
A card created bare and moved afterwards is the Mac's AITD-328.

listId.description:
The list the board was opened from: the card's own list, and where the project's
columns come from.

oneOf.description: When to be reminded about one task, as offsets from its due time.

Which reminders have come due and have not been shown yet.

Read while the app is running. The server owns push and email; this is only what a running
client can notice about a reminder whose time has arrived — see [`crate::reminders`].

The earliest reminder still to come — `{ "reminder": {taskId, title, reminderTime, …} | null }`
— for a shell that schedules its own wake-up (Android's AlarmManager, AATD-21).
Remember that a reminder was shown, so it is not shown again.

Snooze a reminder as iOS does: the task becomes due `minutes` from now (timed), its
`reminderTime` is left alone, and the reminder is shown again then (D24).

The repeat presets, and how this task's repeat describes itself.

The summary comes back as parts with resource keys rather than a sentence — see
[`crate::rows::repeat`], where the reason is written down.

Who this task can be assigned to, in the order the picker shows them.

One rule for every surface: the detail pane, the row picker and later the board all ask
this. On iOS the picker built the list inline, and the board could not offer an AI agent
at all — see [`crate::rows::assignee`].

A shell may hold the inputs ahead of the cache (AITD-461): an editor's unsaved lists, a
task not created yet, people its search found, the agents it keeps. Each one given wins
over what the cache would say.

agents.description: The account's agents as the shell keeps them; the cached ones when absent.

currentUser.description: Who is signed in, as the shell knows them; the account's record when absent.

discovered.description: People found some other way — a scoped search, someone just added by email.

listIds.description: The lists the task is in, as the editor holds them.

taskId.description:
The task, when it exists. Its lists and current assignee come from the cache unless
`listIds` says otherwise.

oneOf.description:
What quick-add's leading control shows before anything is typed, and who it may offer
(task 8aa5732c).

The web's quick-add resolves this in the component — its own copy of "what does this list
assign a new task to", of `getPriorityColor`, and of the three states the control has. Asking
for it means the answer is the same one [`Command::CreateTask`] will act on, because both go
through [`crate::services::list_defaults`]; a picker that previewed one thing and created
another would be worse than no picker.

`list_id` is the list being added to, or `None` for a pseudo-list like My Tasks.

`assignee_id` and `priority` are what the person has already CHOSEN in the picker, in the
same "said at the door beats the list's default" sense as [`Command::CreateTask`] — so the
control is re-asked after every pick rather than the shell deciding which of the three states
a pick produces.

`assignee_id` is `"unassigned"` for "nobody, on purpose", the same spelling a list's
`default_assignee_id` uses for the same meaning, and absent for "nothing chosen yet". A bare
`null` cannot carry that distinction: `Option<Option<String>>` collapses a JSON null to
`None` through serde's derive, which is the trap `changes_from_json` is hand-written to avoid.
The signed-in user.

Whether there is a stored session. Not whether it is still valid — only the server knows
that, and it says so with a 401.
The Outbox's state, for the "not synced yet" indicator.

Whether the live stream is connected: `{ "live": bool }`. Its edges arrive as `stream`
changes.

Forget the cached rows (not the journal, not the credentials) and start the next sync
from scratch. For a shell whose isolation guard caught rows that are not this account's.

The device is back online: writes waiting for the network go now, the delivery loop is
woken, and the live stream starts over. What a shell calls from its reachability monitor.

Drop the live stream and connect again now — after the machine wakes, or the network comes
back — rather than waiting out a backoff chosen while it was down.

What a pressed key means, given what is on screen.

The shell asks rather than knowing, because the bare-key scheme is a cross-platform
contract locked by `contracts/fixtures/shortcuts.json` — including the part that is easiest
to get wrong, which is *when a key is allowed to fire at all*. A shell that dispatched from
its own table would drift from web the first time somebody added a shortcut there.

Pure: no cache, no network, no clock. It is safe to ask on the UI thread while a key is
being handled.
The whole scheme, for a shortcuts sheet.

Which real ids these temporary ones became, once their creates reached the server: an
object from each temp id that has one to the id it is now. Ids with nothing to say are left
out, so an empty answer means "nothing has moved".

Put a write another client's journal already applied on screen into this one, to be sent
as it was: the Apple apps' queued writes, carried over on their first launch through this
crate so an offline edit made before the update still reaches the server.

The cache is not touched — the edit is already in it, from `seedCache` — and the payload is
journaled verbatim, in this journal's own shape for `kind` (`{"body":…}` for `createTask`,
`{"taskId":…,"body":…}` for `updateTask`, and so on). `clientRequestId` is the original
idempotency key, so a write the old journal did send is not made twice.

Fill an empty cache from a shell's own, once, when it starts speaking through this crate —
the Apple apps' Core Data on their first launch after the move — so an offline first launch
still shows everything. Journals nothing and leaves the sync cursor alone: the first pass
still pulls everything, and the server's answer replaces what was seeded.

currentUser.description:
Who is signed in, recorded as sign-in records it — for a UI-test build, which seeds a
signed-in person without ever reaching the server (AATD-18). Absent, nobody changes.

applyListDefaults.description:
Fill what the caller left unsaid from the list's defaults. On unless a shell has already
applied them itself — the Apple apps did, before they spoke through here — or is
importing a task that must arrive exactly as it was (a sync provider's).

keepAssignee.description:
Born in Waiting, a task is unassigned — `assigneeId` and any list default included —
unless this is `true`.

locale.description:
The reader's language tag (`en-US`, `de`, `zh-CN`), for the words the quick-add box
reads out of a sentence. Absent means English.

quickAdd.description:
True when the title was typed into the quick-add box, where the web's smart parsing
reads `#list` tags, dates, repeats and priorities out of it when the account has it
on (task 6ac2639a, CONTRACTS.md D11). A subtask typed into a detail is not parsed, as
it is not on the web.

statusRole.description:
The board status the task is born with: a role, never a list id (task 95c7a68f). `None`
is the Inbox, which is the absence of a status rather than a status of its own.

A card typed into a board column has to arrive WITH its role — created bare and moved
afterwards is the Mac's AITD-328, where the role was dropped in between and every card
appeared in the Inbox. See [`Command::AddBoardCard`], which is how a column asks.

waitOnTaskId.description:
Born in Waiting on a task (`statusRole: "waiting"`): attached as a blocker once the
task exists. A new task has no blockers, so it enters Waiting only with this or a
future `dueDateTime`; with neither the create fails with `WAITING_NEEDS_CONDITION`
and nothing is written (`astrid_rules::waiting`, R2; [`WaitOptions`]).

oneOf.description:
Edit a task. The body is the same shape the API takes, so a field the shell learns about
needs no change here — see [`crate::services::TaskChanges`] for how absent and null differ.

The Waiting rules apply here too (`astrid_rules::waiting`): `statusRole: "waiting"` needs a
condition (a future `dueDateTime` in the same body or already on the task, or an
incomplete blocker) or fails with `WAITING_NEEDS_CONDITION`, and clears the assignee unless
the body says `"keepAssignee": true` or sets `assigneeId` itself. An edit of a Waiting task
that takes away its last condition (clears or passes its date) moves it to Ready.
Complete or un-complete a task. **The only way to do either.**

completedAt.description: When it was completed, if not now: a sync provider backdating a tick made elsewhere.

source.description:
Who completed it — `astrid`, `google`, `github`, `apple` — so a provider can tell its
own echo from a person's tick.

task.description:
The task as the person sees it, in the wire shape, when a view let them edit its due
date or repeat first: the rollover anchors on those fields, and the cache may be a sync
behind (rule 3 of the README).

timerDuration.description: What a timer produced, when the task was completed from one.

oneOf.description:
Close a task as something other than done — `canceled` | `duplicate` | `not_planned` — or
reopen it with `null` (task 016ce981). Not a way to complete one: a canceled close does not
roll a repeating task forward, on purpose.

The board columns a task's menu can put it in, and which one it is in now. The project's
own columns when the task is in a project, the defaults every board shares when not.

Put a task in a column by id from its menu: the same move a dragged card makes, so the two
cannot disagree — including that Done means completed, and that Waiting needs a condition
([`WaitOptions`]).
Mint a link to the task that other people can open, as the web's Share does. Online-only.
Mint a link to a list, as iOS's Share List does (AATD-44). Online-only.
What a share link (`astrid.cc/s/<code>`) opens: `{ targetType, targetId }` (AATD-59).

Copy a task into a list, with or without its comments, as the web's Copy does. The server
makes the copy, so this is online-only; the copy comes back and is cached at once.

The lists a task can be put in, for the detail's list editor (task d3f3b111): the ones it
is in, the ones that match what was typed, and whether to offer creating what was typed.

`asToggles` asks for the Apple pickers' shape (AITD-461, `docs/CONTRACTS.md` D50): every list
a task can be filed in — the ones it is in too, marked selected — in the sidebar's order
(favourites first, then by name), filtered by what was typed, with no cap and no create. An
editor holding unsaved lists sends them as `listIds`; a task not created yet has no `taskId`.

Make a list and put the task in it, in one step — the editor's **Create "…"**. The new
list's colour and privacy are the core's decision, see `rows::list_picks`.

A board's columns (task e5214fba), addressed by the list the board was opened from. The
rules are `crate::board`, locked against the web; a refused write is a bad request with
the web's own message.

What a list's coding-agent settings can be set to (task f44b4a0c): the agents this
account may put on a list, and the repositories its GitHub connection can reach.

What a list has been doing lately (web AWTD-1329, AWTD-1333): new and completed per day,
the median time to complete, the median stay in each board lane, and the top
contributors. Answers the route's `insights` object unchanged.

`days` is 7, 30 or 90 — anything else, or none, is read as 30 rather than refused, so a
picker cannot hold an option the server answers 400 to. `timeZone` is an IANA zone and
should be the machine's, so that days bucket like the reader's own calendar; absent
means UTC.

Set a task's role directly. Into Waiting it follows the same rule as a move —
[`WaitOptions`].

privacy.description: `PRIVATE`, `SHARED` or `PUBLIC`; the server's default when absent.

oneOf.description:
Put a picture from this machine on a list (task 3a913e52): sent through the secure-upload
route with the list as context, then written as the list's `imageUrl`. Online-only, as
the profile photo is; the write that follows goes through the Outbox.

Where a list's picture can be drawn from — a cached local path for a secure file, an
absolute address otherwise — or null when it has none. `updateList` with `imageUrl: null`
removes one. `imageUrl` names the picture directly for a list this store does not hold —
a public one, from `publicLists` — and `listId` is then only the caller's label for it.

The agents that could power `@astrid`, and which one does (task 810e1876): the web's
selector, read from the account's AI preferences. Online-only, like the Agent Hub.

Choose the agent that powers `@astrid`; null leaves the server to pick. Answers the
selector as it now stands.

The public lists anybody may browse and copy (task f6bc59e8), most copied first.
Online-only: the server keeps the catalogue.

Copy a public list, with its tasks, into this account (task f6bc59e8). Online-only: the
server makes the copy, and answers with the new list.

Open **one** public list by its id, for somebody who is not a member of it (task
c5f7d870) — what [`Command::FeedbackListId`] left every client unable to act on, since
[`Command::PublicLists`] is a catalogue with no id argument and [`Command::CopyList`]
leaves a copy in the sidebar.

Answers `{ list, role, canAddTask, canComment }`: the list, and what this reader may do
in it, so a client does not have to work the rule out. Online-only, and **not cached** —
see [`crate::services::ListService::public_list`]. Pair it with
[`Command::FeaturedRows`] for the tasks.

The rows were dragged into this order (task 7883f710). Only the rows that were on screen;
the core completes the list's order and journals it whole.

A featured public list's rows (AATD-46): its tasks fetched from the server (not cached),
with this account's own unsent ones for it, projected as `rowsForList` projects — other
people's tasks read-only, their control copying. `list` is the public list as the shell
holds it, when this account does not.

iOS's reminder triage deck (AATD-54): the reminded task first, then my open tasks due today
or overdue, soonest first, as rows; and the assistant an up-swipe hands a task to.
Tap one person in a multi-assignee picker (AATD-51): add, remove, an agent first, at most 10.

A row dropped in the list's tree (AATD-42): `zone` is `row` (with `targetId`), `line`,
`outdent` or `indent` (with the visible `rowIds`). Writes the new parent when there is one
and answers `{ outcome, parentId }` — `reorderOnly` asks the shell to write the order itself.

authorId.description:
Whose words these are when not the signed-in person's — a comment copied with its task
keeps its author.

clientRequestId.description:
The temporary id of the row the shell already drew for this comment; it becomes the
comment's id until the server answers, and the idempotency key.

fileId.description: A file already on the server, to carry on the comment.

parentCommentId.description: The comment this one answers (task 97c817dd); absent for a top-level comment.

oneOf.description: Change what a comment says. Offline through the Outbox, like posting one.

What the comment box's popup should show for this text and caret (task 3271a0c5): the
trigger the caret is inside, if any, and the rows for it. Positions are UTF-16 units.

Put a chosen row into the text, the way the server will read it back. The row's kind is
`triggerKind`, because `kind` on the wire is the command itself.
One sync pass: push, fetch, apply.
Drain the Outbox without fetching. What a "retry now" button does.
Give every write the server refused another go, then drain. Answers `{ "revived": n }`.
Refresh a task's comments from the server.
Search for people to assign or invite.

taskId.description: The task the person is being found for — the server searches its lists' people.

oneOf.description:
The Agent Hub: every agent, the mode it is set to, and whether it has what it needs.

One command, like the external-sync panel, because a screen that drew the agents before it
knew which had a credential would show "needs setup" on all of them and then correct itself.

Where an account's own agent is told about work.

Answers for an account that has never configured one: the screen builds its event and agent
pickers from this, so there is something to answer with before there is anything to set.
Save where deliveries go, and what is delivered.

regenerateSecret.description: Ask for a new signing secret. The server answers with it once and never again.

oneOf.description:
Fire a `test.ping` at the configured URL.

The only way to know a webhook works: the URL is somebody else's server, and one nothing
has ever reached is a setting that looks configured and is not.

Everything that can act as this account, grouped and reviewed (astrid-web #285).

Read-only, so the panel opens without minting anything. Nothing here answers with a secret:
the server stores a hash and shows plaintext once, at creation.

Stop one connection. `kind` is the path segment the server revokes by; a kind this build
cannot name is refused here rather than sent.

connectionKind.description: Named for the row, not `kind`: that word is the command's own discriminator on the wire.

oneOf.description: One OAuth client, for editing — the connections list knows its id but not its redirect URIs.

Judge a draft as it is typed: the first problem to fix, the grants after a toggle with the
pairing the web applies, the URIs as lines, and the scopes a picker may offer. Pure, and
asked on every edit, so the editor never has to know a rule.

redirectUriText.description: One URI per line, as typed.

toggleGrant.description: A grant to flip before judging, with its pair.

oneOf.description:
Register a client the caller shaped, and answer with the secret shown only this once. A
draft with a problem is refused here and never reaches the server.

redirectUriText.description: One URI per line, as typed.

oneOf.description:
Change a client's redirect URIs. The rest of the draft rides along so the rule that an
authorization-code client keeps a callback applies to an edit too.

redirectUriText.description: One URI per line, as typed.

oneOf.description:
Client credentials for a transport the agents page configures (`githubActions`,
`webhookServer`). The server decides scopes and grant types from the preset.

A user-level access token, for a cloud agent that has to act as this account (AWTD-1312).

Answers with the token in the one form it will ever be readable, so the shell shows it at
once and stores nothing. It is listed and revoked afterwards as an access token, through
`connections` and `revokeConnection`.

`expiresInDays` is 1-365; absent asks for a token that does not expire. `agent` names the
cloud agent the token is for, such as `copilot`.
The agents this account has registered of its own.
Register one. Answers with the credentials the server will show only this once.

listIds.description:
What the agent may see. Absent is every list this account has, which is a bigger grant
than most people mean.

oneOf.description:
Set a registered agent's photo, or clear it back to the default. `photoPath` is a file on
this machine, uploaded first through the route the profile photo uses (AWTD-1628);
`image` is the address of a photo that already lives somewhere. Not both, and neither
clears it. Answers with the image the server settled on, which for a cleared one is the
default rather than nothing.

Start connecting Copilot, or stop.

The same browser hand-off as every other provider: somebody's GitHub password belongs in
their browser.
Change how one agent runs.
Store a key for one service. Straight to the server; never cached here.

Ask the server whether a stored key works. Answers `{ works, error }`: `error` is the
server's reason when the provider refused the key (AWTD-1610), else null.

Which services have a key stored, on its own (AWTD-1610) — the read [`Command::Agents`]
makes as one part of the hub. Answers the server's map, `{ keys: { <serviceId>: { hasKey,
keyPreview, isValid, lastTested, error } } }`; a service with no key is absent. Never the
key. Online-only.

The agents' modes, on its own (AWTD-1610): `{ agents, modes }` as
`/users/me/agent-modes` answers — `agents` the server's mailbox rows (`{ mailbox, email,
mode, locked }`), `modes` the map of mailbox to mode. Online-only.
Whether Copilot is connected, on its own (AWTD-1610): `{ connected }`. Online-only.

The agents this account can assign, mention or chat with (AWTD-1610, iOS
`getAvailableAgents`): `{ agents: [{ id, name, email, image, service }] }`.
`serverRunOnly` narrows to what the server runs itself — what can power the default
assistant (AITD-297). Online-only.

What a list's external sync looks like: what is connected, what it could be linked to,
and what it is linked to.

One command rather than three, because the screen needs all of it before it can draw a
single row — and three round trips to fill one panel is three chances to show it half done.

The account's side of external sync: for each provider, whether it is connected, **which
account it is connected as**, and every list it has linked — both ends of each named
(task 6db679c3).

Account-wide where [`Command::ExternalSync`] is one list's, because that is the shape the
settings screen is: a GitHub Issues section and a Google Tasks section, each headed
"Connected as …" over the list of links.

Google's "New List": make a list on Google and bind it to an Astrid list, in one gesture.

One command because it is one gesture — and because the half-done state (made on Google,
not bound here) is one this has to clean up after itself rather than hand to a client.

name.description: What to call it on Google. The Astrid list's own name, unless somebody typed another.

oneOf.description: The URL to open in a browser to connect a provider.
Mirror a list to a container on the other side.
How Google lists get linked, and what a list made here is called.

How Google lists get linked: one at a time by hand, or all of them.

The choice is the account's, not this machine's, so it follows somebody to their laptop.

suffix.description: Appended to the name of a list made here for a remote one. Absent leaves it alone.

oneOf.description:
Merge a sync ledger built by another store — an Apple client's old UserDefaults, on its
way onto this crate — into the core's, in one transaction (AITD-463).

Merged, never replaced, so running it twice is harmless. Lists are oldest first: that is
the order the tombstone caps (500 own, 5000 server) evict in. Every part may be absent.

excluded.description: Remote lists auto-linking must never offer again.

links.description: Local task → remote twin, so a later deletion knows what to remove.

pending.description: Remote twins still to remove. Each is also tombstoned, as `record_deletion` does.

oneOf.description:
Run one Google pass over every linked list.

GitHub needs no equivalent: a cron on the server does that one, so a list linked here syncs
whether or not this app is running.

Whether the first-run tour has been seen on this machine.

In the cache rather than in the account: it is about this installation — where its hotkey
is, what its palette does — and somebody who has used the app for a year on a laptop still
wants to be told those things the first time they open it on a desktop.
Remember that the tour has been seen.

Everything one box can find: commands, lists, tasks, ranked.

The matcher is the Mac's, character for character — see [`crate::palette`]. The ranking is
what a palette *is*, and two clients that rank differently are two products.
The three numbers on the signed-in account's profile.

The public tasks a profile shares, as rows, with no `userId` meaning your own (task
da326190 — iOS's `UserProfileView` draws this section beneath the three numbers).

Also answers who they are (`id`, `image`, `createdAt`, `isAIAgent`) and their `stats`, so
another person's whole profile is one request (AATD-69).

Answers `isOwnProfile` and the person's `name` rather than a heading: iOS's two titles
("Your Tasks" and "Shared tasks with <name>") are user-facing strings, and a client holds
its own.

Write everything this account has to a file on this machine.

`format` is `json` or `csv`. The path comes from the shell's save dialog, because choosing
where a file goes is the one part of this the core should not decide.

Change the signed-in user's name, photo, or both (task 19fd9289). `photoPath` is a file on
this machine, uploaded first; `image` is the address of a photo already uploaded
(AWTD-1610 — iOS uploads as soon as one is picked). Not both. The answer is the account
screen, redrawn.
Send the verification email again. Answers with the server's message.

Send the verification email for the account's address (AWTD-1610). Answers
`{ message }`, the server's sentence.
Withdraw a pending email change (AWTD-1610). Answers `{ message }`.

Change the signed-in user's email address (task 4c285039). The address changes only when
the link in the mail is followed, so the answer is `verificationRequired` and the server's
sentence — not a new account screen.
The passkeys the account signs in with (task 19fd9289). Online-only.
Rename a passkey. An empty name is refused before any request, as the server would refuse it.
Revoke a passkey.

Begin registering a passkey (task 4c285039). Answers `{ options, sessionId }`: the options
go to the platform authenticator — Credential Manager on Android, Windows Hello here — and
the `sessionId` comes back to [`Command::RegisterPasskey`].

Finish registering a passkey (task 4c285039) with what the authenticator signed.

`attestation` is the platform's registration response, passed through unread: its shape is
the WebAuthn spec's and the server's business, and a core that parsed it would have to be
released again for every field either of them adds.
The contacts this account imported for collaborator suggestions (task 438494c7). Online-only.
Remove every imported contact. Answers with how many went.

Upload the device's contacts for collaborator suggestions, replacing what the server had
(AATD-68, iOS `ContactsService.syncContacts`). Each is `{email, name?, phoneNumber?}` as the
shell read it from the address book; the batching is here. Answers the server's stats, whose
`total` is the account's whole count. Online-only.

Autocomplete over the imported contacts, for adding a member (AWTD-1610). `query` needs
two characters, as the server does; `limit` defaults to 10 (the server caps it at 50);
`excludeListId` leaves out that list's members. Answers `{ results: [{ id, email, name,
phoneNumber, isAstridUser, astridUserName, astridUserImage }] }`. Online-only.

The Astrid users in this account's contacts, mutual ones first (AWTD-1610). `limit`
defaults to 20 (the server caps it at 100). Answers `{ recommended: [{ id, email, name,
image, contactName, isMutual }], stats: { mutual, nonMutual, total } | null, message |
null }`. Online-only.

Delete the account for good. `confirmation` must be the phrase the web requires, typed
exactly; anything else is refused without a request. Signs out afterwards.

The account: who is signed in, and what their reminder settings are.

From the cache, so the screen draws instantly. [`Command::RefreshSettings`] catches it up.
Fetch the account and its settings from the server.

Change the reminder settings.

The fields are the server's — `enablePushReminders`, `dailyDigestTime`, and so on — merged
into what is already stored, so a screen can send one toggle without restating the rest.

Change the account's task defaults or its task-detail layout (task c0f3db19). The fields
are the server's — `emailToTaskEnabled`, `defaultTaskDueOffset`, `defaultDueTime`,
`taskDisplayMode`, `subtaskDisplay`, `smartTaskCreationEnabled` — merged into what is
stored, and refused here when the server would refuse them. Answers with the account screen.

Start timing a task.

The start time goes in the cache rather than in memory, so a timer survives a restart — on
Apple it does not, and a timer left running an hour ago is simply lost.
Stop timing, and record what the session was worth.

The files on a task: its own, and its comments'.

There is no "attach to task" endpoint anywhere — a file reaches a task by being uploaded and
then named by a comment — so this is the only way to answer "what is attached to this?".
Fetch a file's bytes and answer with the path they were written to.

Attach a file from this machine, and post the comment that carries it.

Works offline like everything else. The bytes are copied into a pending directory and the
journal row names the copy — a journal holding a photograph is a journal nobody can read.
See [`crate::services::attachment`].

clientRequestId.description: The comment's own temporary id, as for `postComment`.

fileId.description:
The temporary id the shell already drew the file under (its thumbnail), the name to
send and the type — each defaulting to what the path says.

path.description: A path on this machine, from the file picker.

oneOf.description:
Which look the app wears, and the ones it could.

Per installation rather than per account — a laptop in the evening and a desktop under an
office light are different questions. See [`crate::theme`].
This user's feature flags, from the cache: `projectMode`, `googleTasks`, `taskCost`,
each `true`, `false`, or null when the server has never been asked (web task AWTD-566).

The server's whole flag answer, `{ version, features }` — every flag, rollouts included,
and the version a `featureFlagsUpdated` frame is compared against (AWTD-1610). Asked
fresh; fails offline, where the shell keeps its own copy.
The global quick-add chord: what it is, and its parts for the shell to register.
Choose another chord. Refused, with a reason, when it is not one the shell could register.

Open an editor in the one editing session (`astrid-web/docs/PRODUCT_CONTRACT.md` §6),
committing and closing whatever was open. Answers with the transition: which editor is
now active, and which one the shell must commit or revert. See [`crate::editing`].

Close an editor, committing it. A stale end — an editor `beginEditing` has already handed
off — is ignored, because honouring it would write the old value over the new one's.
Close an editor, reverting it: the only transition that discards.
Close the session, committing whatever was open: navigating away and backgrounding save.
How much of a title a row shows: wrap, two lines or one line (DS19).
Choose how much of a title a row shows. This machine's, like the theme.
The My Tasks entry for the sidebar: the view the app opens on.

What My Tasks is filtered and sorted by.

From the cache, so a screen draws before the network answers; [`Command::RefreshMyTasks`]
is the catch-up.
Fetch My Tasks' filters from the account.
Change what My Tasks is filtered and sorted by, for this account on every device.

filterAssignee.description:
Carried so a write keeps what another client stored; never applied — iOS's My Tasks does
not read it, and its scope already is "assigned to me" (D25).

filterPriority.description: Empty means every priority — see the module note.

oneOf.description:
What is on the clipboard, and which of it somebody meant to attach.

Reading the clipboard is the shell's job; deciding what it means is not — see
[`crate::paste`] for why files beat a rendition of them and why text is left alone.

files.description: Files the board names on disk, in the order it lists them.

imageExtension.description: The format of an image with no file behind it. Absent when there is no image.

oneOf.description:
What a list is filtered and sorted by, and what else it could be.

Answers for My Tasks too, from the account's preferences rather than a list row.

Set one filter on one list.

A separate command rather than an `updateList` from the shell, because where a filter is
written depends on what is being filtered: a list's go on the list, My Tasks' go on the
account. That is a decision, and decisions are not the shell's.

field.description: The field the group names — `filterCompletion`, `sortBy`, and so on.

oneOf.description:
A list's chat, from the cache.

Answers with the channel and the transcript projected — see [`crate::rows::chat`] for what
"mine", "sending" and "nobody said it" mean and why the shell is not asked to decide them.

Fetch the channels and then this list's messages.

Separate from [`Command::Chat`] because opening a conversation should draw instantly from
the cache and catch up afterwards, the same order the task list uses.
Say something. In the transcript before this returns, whatever the network is doing.

clientRequestId.description: The id a shell already drew the message under; see `postComment`.

fileId.description:
A file to carry. With `path`, a file on this device: copied, queued, and uploaded
before the message goes, under this id when it is a temporary one — the id its
thumbnail is already drawn with. Without, a file already on the server.

oneOf.description:
The chat channel for a list, or — with `virtualKey` — for a virtual list such as My Tasks.
From the cache, else from the server, which creates it on first use. Fails offline when
this device has never seen it.

A channel's cached messages in the wire shape, oldest first — for a shell that draws its
own transcript. [`Command::Chat`] is the projected one.

Fetch a page of a channel's history into the cache: the newest, or the one before
`before`. Answers `{ "messages": [the channel, oldest first], "hasMore": bool }`.

Take a message out of this device's transcript; one not yet sent is not sent. Chat has no
delete on the server.
Post, as the agent, an answer this device produced itself. Online only.
Ask the server to answer as Astrid when this device cannot. Online only.

Who a list is shared with, and what this account may do about it.

From the cache — the roster the lists payload carried, or the last refresh — so the
flyout opens at once and opens offline with the list's own name, colour and privacy,
none of which need a connection. Follow it with [`Command::RefreshListMembers`]:
membership is not a local fact, and a roster a day old is how somebody removed last week
is still offered a role.

The same answer, after asking the server for the roster. Fails offline, and the caller
keeps what [`Command::ListMembers`] gave it.

Invite somebody by email.

Membership changes are sent at once, and a refusal fails the command; only a failed
network queues one, answering `{ "queued": true }` with the cache already showing it. An
invitation answers with the `member` it made or the `invitation` waiting.
Withdraw an invitation not yet accepted, by the address it went to.
Change an invitation's role before it is accepted.
Leave a list somebody else owns.

Who the owner may hand this list to — the probe behind the Transfer control. Answers with
one of four states (`services::list::TransferAvailability`), never a bare error.
Hand the list to another member and leave it, in one call.
Every board (project) this account has, from the cache, in the wire shape.
Create a board; the server seeds its status columns. Online only.
Turn a list into a board in one request. Online only.

Delete a board (owner only); its lists are detached, not deleted. Online only. Answers the
server's `{ success, detachedListIds }`.
Fetch what the deployment supports.

The public list this deployment's Report an Issue opens, from the cached capabilities, or
`null` when it names none — then the shell opens the web instead (task `a4352b30`).

The inbox, from the cache: assigned, mentioned, replied, commented, status changed,
completed (web task ab0572cb).
The inbox, after asking the server.

Mark some of it read. In the cache now, on the server now — not journalled; see
`services::notifications`.
Mark all of it read.

Start signing in. Answers with the URL for the shell to open in the browser.

`provider` (`google`, `github`, `sso`) starts that provider on the hand-off page directly,
for a shell that already asked which one — the iOS sign-in screen's buttons. Absent, the
page offers every provider. The server ignores one it cannot start (AATD-3).
Finish signing in, from the URL Windows activated the app with.
Abandon the sign-in in progress — the user closed the browser prompt.
Forget everything: the cache, the journal, the credential.
